subject: physiology
title: Intrinsic Factor, Cobalamin Absorption, and Phases of Secretion

steps.tx: In addition to hydrochloric acid, gastric parietal cells synthesize and secrete the glycoprotein **gastric intrinsic factor**. Intrinsic factor is the sole gastric secretion that is strictly indispensable for life, required for the intestinal absorption of dietary vitamin B12 in the terminal ileum.
steps.say: Gastric intrinsic factor is the only stomach secretion essential for life, necessary for vitamin B12 absorption in the ileum.

left.title: Gastric Acid (HCl)
points: Secreted by parietal cells into gastric lumen
Aids protein denaturation and pepsin activation
Kills ingested pathogens and bacterial contaminants
Dispensed with after total gastrectomy without fatal harm

right.title: Intrinsic Factor (IF)
points: Glycoprotein (44 kDa) secreted in parallel with HCl
Binds dietary cobalamin in alkaline duodenum
Mediates receptor-mediated endocytosis in terminal ileum
Strictly indispensable for life; loss causes fatal anaemia

steps.tx: In the acidic gastric lumen, dietary vitamin B12 released by pepsin binds with highest affinity to salivary haptocorrin, also known as R-protein, protecting cobalamin from acid hydrolysis. In the alkaline duodenum, pancreatic proteases degrade haptocorrin, allowing free cobalamin to bind with **high-affinity intrinsic factor**.
steps.say: Cobalamin binds protective haptocorrin in acid, but transfers to intrinsic factor in the duodenum after pancreatic digestion.

nodes.label: Stomach: Acid and Pepsin Release Dietary B12; B12 Binds Salivary Haptocorrin (R-Protein)
Duodenum: Pancreatic Proteases Degrade Haptocorrin; B12 Transferred to Intrinsic Factor
Terminal Ileum: B12-IF Complex Binds Cubam Receptors; Internalized via Endocytosis
Enterocyte: B12 Cleaved from IF and Exported into Portal Blood Bound to Transcobalamin II

steps.tx: The intrinsic factor-cobalamin complex travels intact through the jejunum until it reaches the specialized brush border of the terminal ileum. Here, the stable complex binds to the apical multiligand endocytic receptor **cubilin-amnionless complex**, initiating calcium-dependent receptor-mediated endocytosis into absorptive ileal enterocytes.
steps.say: The intrinsic factor complex binds cubilin receptors in the terminal ileum, entering enterocytes by endocytosis.

left.title: Receptor-Mediated B12 Uptake
points: Physiological pathway operating at normal dietary intake
Mediated by cubilin-amnionless (Cubam) receptors in terminal ileum
Requires intact intrinsic factor complex and calcium
Saturable transport capacity (~1.5 to 2.0 mcg per meal)

right.title: Passive Mass-Action Diffusion
points: Operates along entire length of small intestine
Independent of intrinsic factor or cubilin receptors
Accounts for ~1% of any large pharmacological oral dose
Permits high-dose oral cobalamin (1000 mcg/day) to treat pernicious anaemia

steps.tx: Autoimmune destruction of gastric parietal cells and circulating autoantibodies against intrinsic factor cause chronic atrophic gastritis and **pernicious anaemia**. The resulting loss of intrinsic factor leads to severe megaloblastic anaemia and subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord due to impaired myelin synthesis.
steps.say: Autoimmune loss of parietal cells causes pernicious anaemia, with megaloblastic changes and spinal cord degeneration.

vis.alt: Autoimmune atrophic gastritis and parietal cell destruction
vis.caption: Parietal cell atrophy, intrinsic factor deficiency, and neuro-haematological consequences of cobalamin malabsorption.

steps.tx: Gastric acid secretion is coordinated in three distinct, overlapping physiological phases. Activated by the sight, smell, thought, or taste of appetizing food, the **cephalic phase of secretion** is mediated exclusively by vagal cholinergic efferents from the medulla, accounting for thirty percent of total meal-stimulated acid secretion.
steps.say: The cephalic phase is driven by vagal cholinergic signals responding to food sensory cues, providing thirty percent of acid output.

nodes.label: Sensory Cues (Sight, Smell, Taste, Chewing) Stimulate Cerebral Cortex and Hypothalamus
Dorsal Motor Nucleus of Vagus Sends Cholinergic Efferents to Gastric Wall
Direct M3 Stimulation of Parietal Cells + GRP Stimulation of Antral G Cells
Cephalic Secretory Surge Accounts for ~30% of Total Postprandial Acid Output

steps.tx: Upon arrival of swallowed food into the gastric cavity, the **gastric phase of secretion** begins, accounting for sixty percent of total acid output. Physical mechanical distension of the gastric corpus stimulates vagovagal reflexes, while partially digested peptides and amino acids directly stimulate antral G cells to release gastrin.
steps.say: The gastric phase produces sixty percent of acid output, stimulated by stomach distension and digested peptides.

rows: Vagus nerve (ACh via M3, GRP on G cells)
Vagovagal reflexes, local ENS arcs, gastrin release
Entero-oxyntin, absorbed amino acids, endocrine signals

steps.tx: When chyme enters the proximal small intestine, the brief **intestinal phase of secretion** is initiated, providing approximately ten percent of total acid output. Driven initially by absorbed circulating amino acids, it is rapidly eclipsed by negative feedback inhibition as acidic, hypertonic chyme triggers enterogastrone release.
steps.say: The intestinal phase briefly accounts for ten percent of acid before hormonal enterogastrones shut down secretion.

vis.alt: Phases of gastric acid secretion and neuroendocrine signaling
vis.caption: Neuroendocrine integration across cephalic, gastric, and intestinal phases of acid secretion.

steps.tx: To prevent duodenal ulceration, acid secretion is terminated by hormonal and neural **negative feedback inhibition of acid**. As gastric luminal pH drops below three, antral D cells release somatostatin, directly inhibiting G cells; furthermore, duodenal acid, fat, and hypertonicity stimulate secretin, cholecystokinin, and gastric inhibitory peptide.
steps.say: Luminal acid stimulates somatostatin and duodenal enterogastrones, shutting down acid secretion to protect the bowel.

nodes.label: Antral Luminal pH Falls Below 3.0 (Excess Free Hydrochloric Acid)
Antral D Cells Secrete Paracrine Somatostatin into Interstitium
Somatostatin Strongly Inhibits G Cell Gastrin Release and ECL Histamine
Enterogastrones (Secretin, CCK, GIP) Complete Feedback Shutdown of Acid Secretion
